note: Operator-approved, published pieces. The calibration set: a gate that rejects one of these is miscalibrated, and test_goldens.py says so.

deviations.post.em_dashes: Drafted before the one-em-dash rule was adopted on 2026-08-24. Two remain. Not edited here: this is the operator's draft, and editing it to pass would fabricate an approval it never got.

deviations.post.hook_words: 20-word hook against the 15-word limit adopted 2026-08-24. The hook is the strongest in the set and shortening it is an editorial decision, not a mechanical one.
deviations.post.body_chars: 1178 characters against the 1400 floor adopted 2026-08-24, when the band moved up from the old 200-260 word rule. The draft predates the move.
deviations.post.markdown: Carries a fenced ASCII table of the reliability arithmetic. LinkedIn renders no Markdown, so the backticks would publish literally. A genuine defect the gate found, not a threshold disagreement — this one should be fixed in the draft rather than tolerated.

deviations.post.em_dashes: Three em dashes against the limit of one, same 2026-08-24 rule. Same reasoning as the RAG post.

deviations_policy: A declared deviation is not a waiver. test_goldens.py asserts a golden fails EXACTLY its declared deviations: a new failure fails the suite, and a deviation that stops firing also fails it, because a stale exception is how a golden set quietly stops being a brake. Every entry names the rule it breaks and why it was not edited away.
